slides.title: Wasit
slides.lede: Protecting advance payments in stablecoin trade.
slides.body: A BTC bond on Mezo stands behind the supplier's production advance. The balance waits in MUSD escrow until named people sign.

slides.title: The advance leaves before the goods exist.

slides.title: Bitcoin behind the advance. The balance waits for signatures.

steps.head: Terms fixed first
steps.text: Buyer, supplier, inspector, carrier, arbiter, amounts, deadlines and a hash of the terms document are set before money moves.

steps.head: BTC bond
steps.text: The supplier or their sourcing agent locks BTC on Mezo, 150% of the net advance in our deals, priced by the Skip BTC/USD feed.

steps.head: Advance to the supplier
steps.text: The buyer pays the advance in MUSD with one permit signature. It goes straight to the supplier for production.

steps.head: Balance on signatures
steps.text: The balance is held in MUSD escrow. It is released after the inspector signs READY, the carrier signs SHIPPED and a challenge window passes.

slides.title: Every exit is written into the deal, and none can be paused.

slides.title: Each deal is MUSD demand from people who trade goods.

items.head: MUSD
items.text: Settlement currency for advance, balance and refunds, paid with EIP-2612 permits.

items.head: BTC on Mezo
items.text: Bond collateral, through BTC's ERC-20 precompile.

items.head: Skip BTC/USD
items.text: Prices the bond, with staleness and bounds checks. A Pyth adapter is implemented and fork-tested.

items.head: Mezo Router
items.text: Turns bond BTC into MUSD on default or protection, with an oracle-bounded minimum.

items.head: Mezo Passport
items.text: Wallet connection in the app. Tested with EVM wallets; Bitcoin wallets not tested yet.

items.head: MUSD borrowing system
items.text: Mapped on testnet for Wave 2: minimum trove debt 2,000 MUSD, liquidation at 110%.

left.head: What the contracts refuse
items: The owner can never move deal funds or bond collateral.
Release, refund, claim and dispute rulings can never be paused.
Refunds from escrow never depend on the bond or its price feed.

right.head: What can still go wrong
items: In a fast BTC crash the bond can fall short of the advance. The app shows coverage at all times.
A signature proves the named person signed. It does not prove the goods shipped.

slides.title: Sourcing agents already vouch for suppliers. Wasit lets them back it.

left.head: First users
items: Sourcing agents who coordinate buyers, factories and inspections, and can post a bond for a supplier who holds no BTC.
Then the importers and suppliers they work with.
Freight forwarders and inspectors, who already sign for goods, in the carrier and inspector roles.

right.head: Business model to test
items: A fee of 0.5% on value actually settled to the supplier. No fee on refunds.
The fee is set on chain and capped by the contract.
No fee has been paid by anyone yet: everything so far ran on testnet.
